title: "typicality experiment"
output: html_notebook
---

# load packages
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library (ggthemes)
library(rstatix)
library(ggpubr)
library(emmeans)
library(dplyr)
```

# import & bind data
```{r}
## compile data for each sona/prolific subject into 2 files
P_subjects = list.files(path ='./data/prolific', recursive = TRUE, pattern = '.csv', full.names = TRUE)
prolific_data <- read_csv(P_subjects) %>% rbind()

S_subjects = list.files(path ='./data/sona', recursive = TRUE, pattern = '.csv', full.names = TRUE)
sona_data <- read_csv(S_subjects) %>% rbind()

## merge sona and prolific data
ncol(prolific_data)
ncol(sona_data)

colnames(prolific_data)
colnames(sona_data)

data <- rbind(prolific_data, sona_data)
```

# basic descriptives
```{r}
## N(initial)
data %>% pull(subject) %>% unique()

## number of trials per subject
data %>% group_by(subject) %>% count()

### caution: subject 'NA'
```
# filtering and accuracy exclusion
```{r}
##exclude filler, practice, and non-picture trials
data <- data %>% filter(typeoftrial=="picture" & !(trialcondition %in% c("filler", "Practice")))

##calculate subject accuracy
data <- data %>% mutate(accuracy=ifelse(correct=="TRUE",1,0))

subject_accuracy <- data %>% group_by(subject) %>% summarise(TaskAccuracy=mean(accuracy))

##exclude subjects with accuracy < 60% & incorrect responses
InaccurateSubjects <- subject_accuracy %>% filter(TaskAccuracy < 0.6)

data <- data %>% filter(!subject %in% InaccurateSubjects) %>% filter(accuracy==1)

##total participants after exclusion: 70
data %>% pull(subject) %>% unique()
```
